## 1. ARG-GEM-09 · Argus Album: the rules for Titan's Phase 2 pro coin photos

**Due:** 2026-11-21 · **State:** delivered 2026-11-18, waiting for its check: do not redo it unless a review reopens it

**Why:** Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.

**What it unlocks:** Argus checks every Phase 2 scan against these rules before it reaches Titan.

**Read first:**
- https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/argus/
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/AI_START_HERE.md

**Do this:**
1. Lighting angle, diffusion, white balance, scale, focus, glare on proof surfaces, both sides, file naming.

**Make:** `argus_gemini_coin-photo-rules_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Argus Album/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below and nothing else`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (integer): row
- `rule` (text): one instruction, e.g. 'light from 10 o'clock at 30 degrees'
- `why` (text): what goes wrong without it
- `setting` (text): the number or setting
- `source` (text): PCGS, NGC, ANA, a numismatic photography book
- `url` (URL): the exact page that shows this row, opened by you today; never a home page or search page
- `quote` (text): the sentence on that page that proves the row, copied word for word (under 300 characters)

**One finished row, as an example (use your own data, never copy this):**

```
{
 "n": 1,
 "rule": "Shoot both sides at the same scale with a ruler or known coin in a test frame",
 "why": "...",
 "setting": "...",
 "source": "PCGS",
 "url": "https://...",
 "quote": "..."
}
```

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the maker's or agency's own site (not a blog, forum, wiki or AI summary).
- [ ] Every quote is copied word for word from that page and is on it now.
- [ ] No row is a copy of another with the names changed.
- [ ] Numbers have their unit in the field name or the unit field, never inside the text.
- [ ] The file is valid JSON (or the exact markdown headings asked for) and is named exactly as asked.

**How many:** 25

**Done when:** 25 rows exactly in the shape, every self-check line true.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude opens 10 rows (or 10 claims) at random and compares them with their source.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field
- a row copied from another row with the names changed
- a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
- a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
- a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
- a guess written as a fact (say 'not found' instead)
- anything about Joseph's own accounts, balances, mail or records beyond what the task names

## 2. ARG-GEM-11 · Argus: every metadata field a Galaxy S24 Ultra writes into its photos, and whether Argus's scrubber removes it

**Due:** 2026-12-03 · **State:** now

**Why:** Argus scrubs EXIF before a photo is shared, but nobody has listed what the S24 Ultra actually embeds (GPS, maker notes, motion-photo trailers, XMP) against what the scrubber strips.

**What it unlocks:** Claude closes every gap the list finds so no location or device detail leaves in a shared photo.

**Read first:**
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/pillars/argus/app.js (the scrubber)
- CIPA DC-008 (Exif 3.0), the Adobe XMP specification, Samsung's own pages on Motion Photos and location tags

**Do this:**
1. List every tag group a Galaxy S24 Ultra JPEG and HEIF photo can carry: EXIF IFD0/ExifIFD/GPS IFD, the Samsung maker note and trailer (motion photo, depth), XMP (including GPano and Samsung namespaces), ICC, thumbnails.
2. For each: what it can reveal (place, time, device, person), the standard's own definition, and the file:line in pillars/argus/app.js that removes it, or 'not removed'.
3. Rank by how much it reveals.

**Make:** `argus_gemini_s24-metadata_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Argus Album/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (integer): row
- `tag` (text): tag or group name
- `container` (text): EXIF / GPS / MakerNote / XMP / trailer / ICC
- `reveals` (text): place / time / device / person / none
- `removed` (text): file:line, or 'not removed'
- `url` (URL): the source page
- `quote` (text): under 300 characters, word for word

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the maker's, agency's or store's own site (never a blog, forum, wiki, reseller, or AI summary).
- [ ] Every quote is copied word for word from that page or PDF page and is there now.
- [ ] Every number has its unit in its own field; anything worked out shows its arithmetic in the field that says 'math'.
- [ ] No row is a copy of another with the names changed.
- [ ] The file is valid JSON (or exactly the Markdown asked for) and is named exactly as asked.

**Done when:** Every tag group, each mapped to the scrubber line that removes it or marked not removed.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude checks 10 file:line claims against app.js and fixes every 'not removed' that reveals place, device or person.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field
- a URL that does not open, is a home page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
- a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens rows at random)
- arithmetic that does not add up when Claude redoes it
- a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
- a guess written as a fact (write 'not stated' and name the page you checked)
